title: Warping and Color-Grading Drone Panoramas: Perspective Warp, Puppet Warp, and RAW Tweaks

date.basis: Embedded creation time provided; transcript does not independently confirm the date.

summary: This instructional video presents a drone panorama processing workflow focused on extreme perspective corrections and color grading. The speaker demonstrates isolating distortion in beam-heavy scenes, applying perspective warp to selected zones, and refining the result with puppet warp to preserve straight lines while exaggerating the intended geometry. The session emphasizes RAW-based local adjustments (whites, color temperature, tint) to recover detail in beams and sky, strategic use of HDR-like tweaks as selective fills, and simulated lighting to enhance depth and focal points. Additional techniques shown include sky cloning for atmosphere, careful edge selections, horizon alignment after stitching, and final cropping. The narrative also notes practical considerations such as DJI stitching behavior, megapixel output, and the challenges of assembling multi-drone panos.

sections.title: Initial approach to peripheral distortion and symmetrical warp
sections.description: Set-up for correcting distortion artifacts that pull beams into the frame; emphasizes applying warp in a symmetrical fashion and processing the entire set identically.

sections.title: Isolating distortion zones and planning perspective changes
sections.description: Explains isolating the beam-laden portions from the rest of the composition so that perspective changes target only the necessary areas (third/beam regions) while leaving mountains untouched.

sections.title: Caution about DJI-stitch-induced trapezoidal distortion
sections.description: Notes that DJI stitching can stretch sides and create wide-angle distortion; introduces the idea of using trapezoid corrections to counteract this effect and prepare for cropping.

sections.title: Puppet Warp for nuanced local adjustments
sections.description: Introduces puppet warp as a refinement tool after perspective warp, with a caveat to preserve straight lines (beams) and to build 'walls' to control how warps propagate.

sections.title: Maintaining beam integrity and selective tightening
sections.description: Reinforces the need to avoid excessive warping of linear features and to adjust only the necessary segments to maintain the dramatic geometry without introducing artifacts.

sections.title: Targeted RAW adjustments for darkened sun zones
sections.description: Switches to RAW for localized correction around sunlit zones, dialing whites and color temperature to bring back detail and color without over-saturating.

sections.title: Selective detail enhancement and HDR as a fill
sections.description: Uses a soft brush to blend in enhanced detail for beams without blowing out highlights. Demonstrates employing HDR/clarity/shadows tweaks as targeted fills to strengthen beam definition while maintaining color fidelity.

sections.title: Simulated light, depth layering, and color grading
sections.description: Explains adding a simulated light source and depth cues to emphasize focal regions; demonstrates selective color grading to push blues in shadows and warmth in mid-tones, while avoiding global color overhaul.

sections.title: Sky adjustments and atmosphere via cloning
sections.description: Demonstrates cloning or patching sky areas to achieve a cohesive mood and smoother transitions across the pano, with attention to preserving natural edge blends.

sections.title: Post-stitch horizon alignment and crop
sections.description: Covers correcting horizon tilt introduced by stitching and final cropping to remove warped portions, ensuring a clean pano frame after alignment.
